title: Acceptance while reading a gate argument
statement: Fix a gate kind $k$, counter $c\in\{0,1,2\}$, Boolean accumulator $b$, Boolean value list $v$, and marked-index list $M$. For every Boolean string $\ell$ and position $j$, the evaluator started in its argument-reading phase with these data accepts exactly when there are a natural number $r$ and a Boolean string $t$ such that $\ell$ consists of $r$ true bits followed by a false bit and then $t$, $j+r<|v|$, and $j+r$ is not marked in $M$. In that case, running from the argument-accumulation phase with counter increased by one, accumulator combined with the value of $v$ at index $j+r$ (using OR for an OR gate and AND otherwise), the updated marked list with $j+r$ added at its front, and position zero, on $t$ also accepts.
